chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to me, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'ada ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Were it not for three things in the son of Adam, nothing would make him bow his head: illness, poverty, and death. They are in him, and indeed he is with them, yet he will not cease boasting.
ai.seo_question: What are the three reasons that cause humans to humble themselves according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate how physical and existential vulnerabilities—illness, poverty, and death—serve as divine mechanisms to curb human arrogance (*kibr*) and induce humility (*tawadu*). This concept aligns with the Shia understanding that these trials are not merely punishments but essential spiritual catalysts that remind humans of their finite nature and dependence on God, preventing them from becoming self-sufficient in their own eyes.
